title: Si/SiO2 Two-Cavity Fabry-Perot Dual-Band Filter with 20 Layers
scientific_hypothesis: A two-cavity Fabry-Perot structure using Si (high-index) and SiO2 (low-index) dielectric layers can achieve dual-band transmission at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm with adequate stopband blocking at 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm, provided both materials have validated dispersion data across the full 3.6-5.2 μm operating range.
design_principle: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter with alternating quarter-wave layers of high and low index transparent materials, computationally optimized to shape dual passbands while maintaining out-of-band blocking. Evidence shows 24-layer 4-cavity filters achieved ~100% transmittance with FWHM ~339 nm in mid-IR.
proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Air (20 finite layers total, alternating Si/SiO2 starting with Si)
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: Si and SiO2 are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
quarter-wave seeding reduces optimization search space
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for Fabry-Perot cavities
Multi-cavity coupling produces square-shaped passband profiles
High index contrast (Si n~3.4, SiO2 n~1.45) enables strong blocking with fewer layers
expected_advantages: Si/SiO2 is a widely available material pair in thin-film databases
High index contrast reduces required layer count for adequate blocking
20 layers provides margin below 24-layer constraint for potential refinement
known_risks: Si may have absorption features in mid-IR that reduce peak transmittance
SiO2 dispersion data may not extend to 5.2 μm in some registries
Dual-band optimization may require more than 2 cavities for adequate separation
execution_request_english: Design a 20-layer dielectric multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate for dual-band infrared transmission. Stack topology: CaF2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Air (20 finite layers, alternating starting with Si). Initialize thicknesses using quarter-wave scaling at λ_target=4.45 μm: t_Si = 4450/(4*n_Si), t_SiO2 = 4450/(4*n_SiO2), constrained to [0.75*t_q, 1.25*t_q] with bounds [100, 800] nm. Before TMM execution, verify both Si and SiO2 have ≥3 validated dispersion data points within 3600-5200 nm range. Optimize layer thicknesses to maximize mean transmittance in passbands (4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm) and minimize mean transmittance in stopbands (3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm) at normal incidence in air. Use coherent TMM with smatrix solver. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates count, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Previous route_03 iterations failed due to material_data issues with Ge/ZnS and ThSi2/YbF3 pairs. This refinement switches to Si/SiO2, a more commonly available material pair in thin-film databases, while preserving the multi-cavity Fabry-Perot design principle. Added pre-execution material validation check requiring ≥3 dispersion data points per material in the operating range.
